best_for: Home users who want mail, calendar and contacts for two accounts in one desktop app, and small-business staff who will pay per device to replace Outlook.

points.title: Free covers two accounts at home
points.text: The free license is for home use on one device and two email accounts, and you register to get it. It includes calendar, contacts and tasks. Commercial use is not allowed, and help comes only from the community forum.

points.title: Personal and Business plans
points.text: Personal is USD 49.95 per year or USD 74.95 once, for one person on up to 3 devices with unlimited accounts. Business is USD 59.95 per year or USD 89.95 once, per device. A one-time license covers the current major version unless you add Lifetime Upgrades. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Encryption built in
points.text: You can sign and encrypt messages with PGP or S/MIME without a separate plug-in. Settings sync through eM Sync, which the company describes as end-to-end encrypted.

points.title: More than mail
points.text: It handles Google Workspace, Office 365, Outlook.com and Exchange accounts, and adds notes, chat, message translation and a spell checker. The yearly plans include the AI add-on for summaries and drafted replies.

points.title: Try before paying
points.text: Personal comes with a 30-day free trial and a 30-day money-back guarantee. Schools, universities and non-profits get 30% off. The phone apps are free and need no license.

points.title: Newer systems only
points.text: The Windows packages are MSIX files for x86, x64 and Arm64 and need Windows 10 version 1809 or later; the listing keeps 66 versions. The Mac build is a universal installer that needs macOS 14 or later, and only the current release is listed.
